findings.title: Windows orphan closure is real but delayed and depends on a POSIX remote; not equivalent to the supervisor it replaces
findings.evidence: Orderly teardown kills ssh.exe directly (native effects.zig:4852 NtTerminateProcess on the direct child, which on Windows IS ssh.exe since supervise_posix=false removes the /bin/sh wrapper). On hard desktop crash the remote command still self-closes because healthy() probes the in-process hook server (hook_server.zig:363, dies with the desktop): forced health-failure loop exits 75 after 3 missed probes (~6s, measured). owner_alive/$PPID tracks the REMOTE sshd session, not the local desktop, so it does not fire on local client death; the health probe is the actual closing mechanism, not the PPID logic the PR comment implies.
findings.user_impact: Remote port held ~6s longer than POSIX after a crash. Not an orphan leak.

issue_candidates.title: tunnelArgv is the only runtime-dir-creating builder without chmod 700
issue_candidates.evidence: remote_ssh.zig:294 mkdir -p "$runtime" with no chmod, vs quiesce/token/watcher which all got it. Currently unreachable-as-a-defect because the state machine forces probe->quiesce->tunnel (remote_runtime.zig:461,470) and quiesce must exit 0 first, so the dir is already 700. Fragile: it relies on op ordering, not on the builder being self-sufficient.
